articles.body: At least 17 streets in Baltimore were paved with recycled glass, creating road surfaces that could sparkle when sunlight or streetlights hit them. Baltimore's approach is part of a broader practice of using crushed waste glass in asphalt mixes. Properly processed glass can replace some of the conventional aggregate used in road construction.Wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have performed well. According to the Federal Highway Administration, recycled glass has also been used in road projects elsewhere in the United States. New York City used about 225,000 metric tonnes of glass in resurfacing applications between 1990 and 1995.However, earlier projects found problems when glass was used in high percentages or as large pieces. The guidance recommends using properly processed glass in suitable proportions for asphalt paving.How did Baltimore’s recycled glass roads create a sparkling effectWaste glass was tested for use in hot mix asphalt during field demonstrations in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Test paving strips were placed at about 33 locations across the United States and Canada. Baltimore later used glass in at least 17 streets, producing a sparkle effect from reflected sunlight or street lamp light.Early projects often used more than 25% glass and coarse particles. The guidance says high glass percentages and large particles probably contributed to stripping and raveling problems reported during those demonstrations. Glass does not absorb asphalt cement binder and bonds poorly to it. Moisture damage can become a concern when high percentages and large gradations are used in surface mixes.How is crushed glass turned into a paving materialAccording to the FHWA guidance, turning waste glass into a suitable paving material requires several processing steps before it can be mixed into the asphalt. Waste glass is first cleaned to remove materials such as metal, plastic, and paper. It is then crushed and screened to produce smaller, more suitable pieces while removing flat, elongated, and sharp-edged particles.For surface pavements, the guidance recommends using glass smaller than 4.75 mm, or the No. 4 sieve, as a fine aggregate mixed with conventional materials. Asphalt wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have shown satisfactory performance. Higher proportions, potentially up to 25%, may be suitable for base or binder courses, where the glass is not exposed directly at the road surface.Crushed glass can affect the strength and performance of asphaltWell-crushed glass can also affect the performance of asphalt mixes because of its angular shape and high friction angle. The guidance says these properties can contribute to good lateral stability, with tests reporting stability comparable to, and in many cases better than, conventional mixes. Waste glass also has a specific gravity about 10 to 15% below that of conventional aggregates, which can increase the yield of an asphalt mix.Its low thermal conductivity may also help mixes containing glass retain heat for longer. Skid resistance tests on pavements containing waste glass have produced results within recommended limits. However, larger glass particles measuring more than 19 mm can become slippery when wet and should not be used in surface mixes. The guidance also notes that using more than 15% glass can increase pavement reflectivity and glare, particularly when the surface is wet.What makes recycled glass suitable for asphalt pavingAsphalt mixes containing crushed glass can be designed using standard laboratory procedures. The guidance recommends testing the mix for stripping potential and says conventional pavement structural design methods are appropriate.Most highway departments allow 5 to 10% glass. The guidance says performance is generally best when crushed glass is used as a sand or fine aggregate substitute.The same methods and equipment can be used to store, mix, place, and compact asphalt containing waste glass. Field testing should follow the procedures used for conventional hot mix asphalt. The guidance identifies a need for uniform specifications covering sizing, debris levels, and mix limitations. It says a lack of adequate and consistent glass supply remains a major constraint on wider use.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das have been placed under preventive arrest and will be produced before an executive magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station on Saturday, Delhi Police said.The development comes amid heightened security in the national capital ahead of the party’s proposed ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Delhi Police had denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing law-and-order concerns, public safety and possible inconvenience to residents. The party had planned to demand Kumar’s resignation and the scrapping of the SIR exercise.CJP’s legal head Ratna Singh, in a post on X, said the three leaders would be produced before the executive magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9am.“Abhijeet, Ashutosh and Saurav will be produced before the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM today,” Singh wrote, adding that a Delhi Police official had informed her about the development that morning. She said she would be present at the police station along with other advocates representing the party.CJP leaders detained at Delhi airportDipke, Ranka and Das were detained by Delhi Police after their Delhi-bound flight from Mumbai landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday.The action came before the planned protest, with police personnel entering the aircraft to take the leaders into custody.In a video from the flight, Dipke was seen questioning the police action and challenging officers to arrest him. He also questioned the grounds for the detention, while slogans including “Bharat Mata ki Jai” and “Inquilab Zindabad” were raised.The CJP leaders had earlier said they were prepared to face arrest but would continue their campaign over the electoral roll revision exercise.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Lockheed unveils new Patriot interceptor to counter hypersonic missiles
articles.summary: Lockheed Martin has unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a new interceptor designed to counter hypersonic and other advanced missile threats, as the US races to
articles.body: Lockheed Martin has unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a new interceptor designed to counter hypersonic and other advanced missile threats, as the US races to strengthen its missile defences and replenish stockpiles strained by ongoing conflicts.The new weapon aims to improve the Patriot missile defence system’s ability to engage difficult targets at longer ranges and higher altitudes.According to Reuters, PAC-3 Edge features a new seeker, upgraded flight controls and a multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman.These upgrades are intended to improve the interceptor’s ability to track and engage advanced aerial threats, including hypersonic weapons.Lockheed Martin expects the new interceptor to cost roughly the same as its existing Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (PAC-3 MSE), the report said.The interceptor is being developed under the US Army’s competitive Future Interceptor programme, with Lockheed Martin targeting testing in 2027 and deployment in 2031. The programme reflects Washington’s push to develop defences capable of dealing with increasingly sophisticated missile threats.Intercepting a hypersonic missileIntercepting hypersonic missiles is a major challenge for modern air defence systems. Travelling at more than Mach 5, these weapons can manoeuvre mid-flight, making their trajectories difficult to predict.PAC-3 Edge is designed to counter this challenge with an upgraded seeker to track targets, improved flight controls for manoeuvrability and a multi-pulse rocket motor to provide thrust at different stages of flight.Together, these features aim to improve the interceptor’s ability to engage fast-moving, manoeuvrable threats, though its effectiveness against hypersonic weapons remains to be established through testing.The development of PAC-3 Edge comes as the US seeks to expand interceptor production amid rising demand for air defence weapons.In July, the US Army awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to ramp up production of its existing PAC-3 interceptors, Reuters reported.The company aims to increase annual production capacity from around 600 interceptors to 2,000, reflecting Washington’s push to replenish inventories while meeting the needs of its own forces and allies.

articles.title: 'Ambani won't go out of business': Elon Musk says Starlink competition would benefit Indians
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Sunday said that competition from Starlink would \"benefit Indian consumers\" by offering them more choices, arguing that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Sunday said that competition from Starlink would "benefit Indian consumers" by offering them more choices, arguing that Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani would not go out of business even if his profits declined.In a post on X, Musk criticised what he described as arguments made by Ambani’s supporters against Starlink’s entry into India, calling them “absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole”.“On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor!” Musk wrote.“The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” he added.Musk also argued that Starlink would have to make its services affordable to attract customers. “And, obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable,” he said.Musk’s latest remarks come amid a dispute over the delay in Starlink’s commercial rollout in India. On Friday, he took a swipe at Ambani, addressing him as “Prime Minister Ambani” and alleging that he was the “real boss of India”.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote in an earlier post.He has also alleged that unnamed business groups are trying to obstruct Starlink’s entry to protect their market positions. The government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay is linked to pending regulatory and security requirements.At the India Mobile Congress 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences: Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink.However, the government has said security clearances remain pending for the licensed operators. The satellite spectrum pricing framework is also being finalised, and commercial services can begin once the prescribed requirements are met.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Turkey bans social media for under-15s from November 1
articles.summary: Turkey has formally announced a ban on social media use by children under 15, with the restrictions set to take effect on November 1.
articles.body: Turkey has formally announced a ban on social media use by children under 15, with the restrictions set to take effect on November 1.The decision was published in the official state journal on Saturday, October 10, following the passage of a law by parliament in April. Under the legislation, social media providers must introduce safeguards to protect young users, including age-verification measures.The law requires platforms to “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement” protections for children. It also states that “no service likely to produce an addictive effect in children may be offered”.Turkey joins countries tightening social media rulesTurkey’s move comes amid growing international efforts to limit children’s exposure to potentially harmful online content and platform features.Australia has introduced restrictions on social media use by children, while Britain and France are among the countries pushing for similar measures.Governments backing such restrictions have cited concerns over screen addiction, sleep deprivation, online bullying and eating disorders among young people.The new restrictions come amid concerns raised by rights groups over freedom of expression in Turkey, particularly regarding LGBTQ communities, the media and the political opposition.You use AI every day. articles.title: WA Bravery Awards honour Perth father who rescued his three-year-old daughter from a swimming pool and performed CPR to help save her life
articles.summary: A family holiday in Broome, Western Australia, turned into a life-threatening emergency for Perth father Sandy Spratt in August 2025.
articles.body: A family holiday in Broome, Western Australia, turned into a life-threatening emergency for Perth father Sandy Spratt in August 2025. The 25-year-old was visiting a relative’s home when he noticed an unsettling silence as his two young daughters played near a gated swimming pool. He rushed over and found his three-year-old daughter, Adaleena, unconscious and floating face-down in the water. Spratt pulled her out and immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), helping restore her consciousness before paramedics arrived. After Adaleena made a full recovery, Spratt received recognition at the 2026 Royal Life Saving WA Bravery Awards, using the experience to encourage others to learn first aid.Sandy Spratt heard an alarming silence near the swimming poolSpratt was visiting a family member’s home in Broome in August 2025, during a holiday roughly 2,080 kilometres north of Perth. His two young daughters were playing near a gated backyard swimming pool while he caught up with relatives. The situation appeared ordinary until he noticed that the girls’ laughter had suddenly stopped. Concerned, he ran towards the pool and discovered Adaleena, his three-year-old daughter, unconscious and floating face-down in the water.Spratt immediately pulled her from the pool. The sudden change from a family gathering to a medical emergency left little time for hesitation, and his response would prove critical to his daughter’s survival. The incident later became the reason for his recognition at Western Australia’s Royal Life Saving Bravery Awards.He performed CPR before paramedics arrivedAfter pulling Adaleena from the water, Spratt immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or CPR. According to the ABC News report by Natasha Clark, his daughter regained consciousness before paramedics arrived.Spratt credited his ability to respond instinctively to first aid training he had completed through a previous job. Reflecting on the emergency, he explained that he already knew what to do without having to think about it.Adaleena was taken to Broome Hospital, where she spent time recovering. She subsequently made a full recovery, turning what could have been a devastating family tragedy into a story about the importance of recognising an emergency and acting quickly. Spratt later said the experience reinforced his belief that first aid knowledge could make a difference when someone’s life was at risk.Royal Life Saving WA recognised his quick thinkingSpratt received a Royal Life Saving WA Bravery Award on 9 October 2026, joining dozens of other West Australians recognised for acts of bravery. He was one of 84 people honoured at the 2026 awards.Royal Life Saving WA acknowledged that his ability to recognise the emergency and immediately begin CPR provided Adaleena with essential lifesaving care. The organisation also highlighted the importance of being prepared for emergencies involving children around water.Chief executive Peter Leaversuch said the people recognised through the awards had demonstrated bravery and quick thinking. He emphasised that lifesaving skills were not exclusive to professional lifeguards or emergency responders. Spratt’s recognition therefore reflected not only his actions as a father, but also the practical value of knowing how to respond when an emergency develops unexpectedly.Unfamiliar swimming pools can pose risks during holidaysRoyal Life Saving WA used the incident to highlight the dangers children can face around swimming pools in unfamiliar surroundings. During holidays, families may spend time at relatives’ homes or in accommodation with pools that children do not regularly encounter.The organisation warned that unfamiliar aquatic environments can create unexpected risks, making close supervision particularly important. Even when a pool is gated, adults should remain attentive to children around water and be prepared to respond if something goes wrong.Spratt’s experience illustrates how quickly a seemingly routine family visit can change. The sudden silence that alerted him to the emergency was followed by an immediate rescue and CPR, with his earlier training helping him act without hesitation. The case also reinforces the value of learning first aid before an emergency occurs, rather than waiting until someone needs help.The father wants others to learn lifesaving skillsFor Spratt, the award offered an opportunity to share a message beyond his own family’s experience. He has encouraged people to complete first aid courses and learn CPR, crediting the training he received through a former job with helping him save Adaleena’s life.“Doing a first aid course really does save lives and is worth every bit,” he said, according to the ABC report.His message echoes that of Royal Life Saving WA, which hopes stories recognised through the awards will encourage more people to acquire lifesaving skills. Although no one wants to face an emergency involving a loved one, knowing how to respond can be crucial while professional help is on its way. Adaleena’s recovery and Spratt’s recognition have given the family a reason to speak publicly about preparedness, quick thinking and the importance of first aid knowledge.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Wilbur the pig went from wandering through a West Hollywood neighbourhood to becoming the unlikely focus of an adoption contest.
articles.body: Wilbur the pig went from wandering through a West Hollywood neighbourhood to becoming the unlikely focus of an adoption contest. After his appearance was captured on video and spread online, the pig was taken to the West L.A. Animal Shelter, where no owner came forward. Four people eventually expressed interest in adopting him, prompting a silent auction. As reported by ABC news, the winning bid came from Marcia Zwilling, managing director of the Diane Warren Foundation, on behalf of Oscar-nominated songwriter Diane Warren. Warren had seen footage of Wilbur and wanted him somewhere safe. He will now move to her seven-acre Malibu sanctuary, joining other rescued animals.Wilbur the pig attracts four hopeful adopters after his West Hollywood rescueWilbur was first noticed wandering through a West Hollywood neighbourhood, where his unexpected appearance was captured on video. The footage circulated widely, turning the loose pig into a familiar sight to people following the story.His journey changed when he was safely taken to the West L.A. Animal Shelter. Staff waited for an owner to claim him, but nobody came forward. That left the shelter facing a rather unusual adoption situation as word about the pig continued to spread.By Thursday, four people had arrived with hopes of adopting Wilbur. With more than one prospective home interested, the shelter used a silent auction to decide who would take responsibility for him.Diane Warren wins bid to give Wilbur a new home at her Malibu sanctuaryThe successful bid was made by Marcia Zwilling, managing director of the Diane Warren Foundation. She was acting on behalf of Warren, the songwriter behind numerous film songs and a 17-time Oscar nominee. According to Zwilling, Warren had seen news footage of Wilbur running through West Hollywood and immediately wanted to help. She contacted Zwilling with a simple request."Diane saw the news clips and saw the little pig running in West Hollywood and she just called me and said, 'Please get the pig, get the pig!"For Wilbur, that meant a move from the animal shelter to a very different setting. He is now headed for Warren’s seven-acre sanctuary in Malibu, where he will live alongside other rescued animals.A seven-acre sanctuary in MalibuThe sanctuary is intended to give Wilbur plenty of space and company. Zwilling said he will have other animal companions around him and will be fed what she described as gourmet salads. There is also a small complication with his name. Warren already has another pig called Wilbur at the sanctuary, meaning the new arrival may eventually be given a different one.Warren has suggested “Hollywood” as a possible replacement, a fitting reference to the place where the pig first became known.Warren jokes about her Oscar recordWarren has spent much of her career writing songs for films and has received 17 Oscar nominations without winning the Academy Award. Her reaction to Wilbur’s arrival was characteristically light-hearted. “I lose Oscars but I won a pig,” Warren said.The remark came as Wilbur’s unusual journey reached its final stage. What began with a pig appearing unexpectedly on West Hollywood streets ended with him being claimed through an auction and given a permanent home at a private animal sanctuary.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India on Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India on Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured more than 300.“We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property,” the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.“We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons. The repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately,” it added.India also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying it stood with the country and its people in defending their sovereignty and hoped peace and normalcy would return to the region soon.Meanwhile, the US also condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airport.Asked whether Washington had decided to join the strikes against the Houthis in Saudi Arabia, US President Donald Trump said, “We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly.”He added, “Look, the Saudis are good fighters. But I think the attack was a terrible thing.”King Khalid International Airport has faced multiple attacks over the past week, following the launch of a major military offensive by a Saudi-led coalition against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen.Earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7 reportedly killed three people and injured 36, according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).Following the latest attack, airport operations were temporarily suspended and travellers were evacuated. Dozens of ambulances were seen rushing to the site.The airport also issued an alert asking passengers to check their flight status with airlines before leaving for the airport.According to flight-tracking platform Flightradar24, flights heading to Riyadh were being diverted to other destinations nearly four hours after the last flight landed at 2.05 pm local time. articles.title: Using AI models, scientists are trying to do a Jurassic Park; bring back to Earth extinct Grey Wolf pups and Woolly mammoths
articles.summary: The aim of bringing long-lost creatures back from the dead has jumped from the silver screen into modern laboratories.
articles.body: The aim of bringing long-lost creatures back from the dead has jumped from the silver screen into modern laboratories. Through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, CRISPR gene editing and ancient DNA extraction, Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths, drawing frequent comparisons to Jurassic Park. Speaking with CNBC, Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line between cinema and science.“I think anyone that saw Jurassic Park in the 90s and didn’t say it was cool, like I don’t think they’re probably very fun at parties,” Lamm joked, adding, “But yes, I saw the movies. I love them. They entertained us. They scared us. I constantly have to remind people on X that, you know, they were movies. I don’t think Jurassic Park had any conservation or general human benefit models to it, so we’ve tried to take a slightly different perspective.”Since viable dinosaur DNA degrades and cannot survive across tens of millions of years, reviving dinosaurs remains physically impossible. However, Colossal has set its sights on species lost to more recent history, including the dire wolf, the woolly mammoth, the dodo bird, the Tasmanian tiger, and the giant New Zealand moa bird.“It’s highly likely in the next coming year or two, people will continue to see us deliver extinct species back to Earth, and we could even have more dire wolves, too,” Lamm noted.How AI reconstructed extinct wolf genomeTo engineer its first generation of dire wolf pups, scientists extracted fragmented genetic material from a fossilised skull and tooth dating back thousands of years. Since ancient DNA is naturally fractured and degraded, Colossal deployed advanced AI models to piece together the broken sequence, successfully reconstructing the complete dire wolf genome. Scientists then mapped the computational blueprint against the genetic code of the gray wolf, the animal’s closest living relative.From there, researchers edited living cells from modern gray wolves to generate viable embryos. Three pups, named Romulus, Remus and Khaleesi, were carried and delivered by domestic dogs serving as surrogate mothers. Born on October 1, 2024, in North Texas, Romulus and Remus represent the first successful lineage bred from DNA fossils of an animal that vanished more than 12,500 years ago.When critics argue that the pups are technically genetically modified gray wolves rather than authentic dire wolves, Lamm dismissed the debate as a semantic distraction.“Gray wolves are just genetically modified dire wolves. They were just done by nature or God or however you want to classify it,” Lamm said, calling the objection an argument that “misses the forest for the trees.”Engineering Woolly Mammoths for ecological restorationColossal is applying a parallel approach to its high-profile woolly mammoth project, which involves inserting mammoth cold-weather traits into the cells of modern Asian elephants. The company is targeting its first mammoth birth sometime in the 2030s.“We call it a woolly mammoth. Because if it looks like a duck, it quacks like a duck, it serves ecological functions of a duck, it’s a duck, in our perspective,” Lamm said.The initiative traces back to 2019, when Lamm met renowned Harvard geneticist George Church, widely considered the father of synthetic biology. Church had long envisioned using CRISPR to bring back extinct fauna as a proving ground for human medicine and programmable biology.Beyond curiosity, Lamm points to direct climate benefits. First of those is Arctic Permafrost Preservation wherein herds of heavy mammoths could compact dense snow blankets across high-latitude Arctic zones, allowing freezing air to penetrate deep into the ground and keeping permafrost locked solid.Secondly, by felling trees and trampling shrubs, the animals could help transform heat-absorbing forests back into reflective tundra grasslands.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Stringent traffic restrictions remained in force across several parts of Delhi on Sunday for a second consecutive day as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) renewed its call for protests demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. articles.title: Christie Brinkley turned a 20-acre Hamptons estate into a private 'castle' with a greenhouse, pond and rewilded grounds
articles.summary: Christie Brinkley has spent more than two decades transforming her Bridgehampton estate into a private retreat that combines historic architecture with
articles.body: Christie Brinkley has spent more than two decades transforming her Bridgehampton estate into a private retreat that combines historic architecture with gardens, open grounds and unique features. Known as Tower Hill Estate, the property covers more than 20 acres and includes bedrooms, bathrooms across its main house and other buildings. Realtor reported that Brinkley gave real estate influencer Caleb Simpson a rare tour of the property, showing the spaces and outdoor areas that have made the estate one of the Hamptons’ distinctive homes.Christie Brinkley’s 20-acre Hamptons estate looks like a castleThe property’s castle-like appearance comes largely from its distinctive turret, which rises from the centre of the main residence. During the tour covered by Realtor, Simpson pointed out how the tower gives the house its castle appearance, while Brinkley herself described it more modestly as a little storybook house.Tower Hill Estate dates back to 1891, when it was built by local resident Dr John Gardiner. Brinkley bought the property in 1998, more than a century after it was constructed. Realtor noted that the house has since been restored with meticulous care, preserving its historic character while allowing it to function as a family home.The estate is spread across three parcels and contains considerably more than the main residence. The compound includes a 4-bedroom, 5-bathroom main house, a 4-bedroom guesthouse with two and a half bathrooms, a barn and art studio with living quarters, a four-car heated garage and a 50-foot observation deck.What makes the grounds different from a typical Hamptons estateBrinkley has given the land as much attention as the buildings. Realtor reported that she raises chickens on the property and is in the process of rewilding the grounds so that more flowers can grow across the estate.That approach is visible around the house, where the lawns and gardens form a major part of the setting. The original property listing described the grounds as park-like, with old specimen trees, winding walking paths and hills used for winter sledding. A private pond also forms part of the landscape, adding another natural feature to the expansive property.The estate also has a greenhouse with its own fireplace. During the tour, Brinkley showed the greenhouse and areas around the pool, where flower-filled planters add colour to the surroundings. She explained that the yard becomes filled with flowers in spring as the rewilding work continues.Why the estate feels like more than a historic houseThe property combines its old-world appearance with spaces designed for everyday family life. Inside, Realtor described soaring ceilings, large windows and plenty of natural light. The home includes an oversized country kitchen, a double-height great room, living and family rooms, three fireplaces, a gym and an office.A wisteria-covered pergola and multilevel stone terraces extend the living areas outdoors. There is also a heated pool with a spa, while the hidden tennis court gives the large estate another private recreational space.The interiors are not presented as a formal museum-like setting. Instead, Brinkley has filled the house with personal possessions and playful decorative touches. The dining room, for example, has a large round table, built-in storage, a bay window, chandeliers and paper lanterns, along with a neon dining room sign.How has Brinkley made the house feel personalThe tour also revealed several objects that reflect Brinkley’s personal connection with the property. Realtor reported that she showed a Broadway playbill that she considers her favourite cover she has ever done. She also pointed out a 270-year-old bonsai tree, joking about its age during the tour.The home has also been used for family gatherings. Brinkley showed the area where the family eats Thanksgiving dinner, giving the enormous property a more lived-in character despite its scale.The main residence is not the only place where the estate’s personality appears. The chickens that Brinkley keeps on the grounds have individual names, including Scrambled, Sunnyside Up and Benedict, adding an unexpectedly domestic touch to the sprawling property.What happened when Brinkley put the estate on the marketBrinkley has not always planned to remain at Tower Hill Estate. After owning the Bridgehampton property for about 20 years, she listed it in 2016 for $29.5 million. Realtor reported that she also put her Sag Harbor home on the market at the same time.The listings were part of an experiment. Brinkley planned to continue living in whichever of the two properties did not sell. Her Sag Harbor residence eventually found a buyer in February 2019, selling for just under its discounted $17.5 million asking price.That left Tower Hill Estate as her remaining Hamptons home. By the time of the Realtor report, Brinkley had lived there for 24 years and described it as the longest she had lived anywhere in her life.The observation tower provides perhaps the clearest reason the property has acquired its castle-like reputation. Rising above the main house, the turret offers wide views of the surrounding area and provides a final stop on Brinkley’s tour. The original listing also highlighted views extending towards the Atlantic Ocean and Connecticut Shore.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Maintain peace for 1 year': CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka released from detention
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An executive magistrate court on Sunday released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An executive magistrate court on Sunday released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from detention, a day after Delhi Police detained them following their arrival in the national capital ahead of a planned protest at Jantar Mantar.They were released on condition that they would not "breach peace" for a year, CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said.Advocate Soutik Banerjee also confirmed their release, saying, “All three (Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das) have been released. They can go from here.”Delhi Police said the three leaders were preventively arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) on October 10. They were produced before the Sub-Divisional Executive Magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi Cantonment on Sunday, police said.“All due legal procedures were followed,” Delhi Police said, adding that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished to ensure peace and good behaviour for one year, following which the court released them.In a post on X after their release, CJP said, “Finally Delhi Police is forced to release Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das.”“Cockroaches never die,” the party added.The three leaders were detained by Delhi Police immediately after their flight landed in the national capital on Saturday and were subsequently placed under preventive arrest ahead of the planned protest at Jantar Mantar, police said.The detentions came amid a major security clampdown in Delhi. More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, preventing them from reaching Jantar Mantar, police sources said.Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.The CJP renewed its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday as police continued security arrangements across the city. articles.title: Debt, abuse and restricted movement: 14 rescued from farms in suspected bonded labour cases in Rajasthan
articles.summary: 14 people, including eight minors, were rescued from farms in Nagaur, Bikaner and Ajmer in suspected bonded labour cases, alleging debt traps, abuse and restricted movement.
articles.body: Jaipur: Fourteen people, including eight minors, were rescued in three suspected bonded labour cases in Nagaur, Bikaner and Ajmer within one week in Sept this year. Families alleged that they were trapped in debt and not allowed to leave farms. They also reported verbal abuse, physical assault and children being forced to work.The families had migrated from their hometowns in search of work. They were rescued following complaints filed by their relatives.This year India marks 50 years of the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, with govt aiming to identify and release all bonded labourers by 2030.In Nagaur, six family members, including four children, were rescued from a farm in Chappri village, Merta, on Sept 26. They belonged to Jayal in Nagaur and Bhopalgarh in Jodhpur.Ramniwas Nayak said his family had taken an advance of Rs 1.5 lakh, but outstanding debt allegedly rose to Rs 2.45 lakh over 1.5 years despite five family members working on the farm.“Pabandi puri thi, kahi aane jaane nahi deta,” he said, alleging that the owner restricted their movement, threatened them with a gun and prevented them from attending even family funerals. He also alleged that the owner assaulted him on Sept 24. This led to a complaint by Ramniwas’s brother on Sept 25.SDM Sunil Kumar said an investigation was underway and further action would follow if a bonded labour case was established.In Bikaner, six members of a family from Anupgarh, Sri Ganganagar, were rescued from a farm in Akhoosar on Sept 29. The family included three minors.Hariram said his family worked on a farm for nearly five years, but he could never repay the debt as the employer kept adding other expenses to the loan. “My employer would sell crops I grew and never gave me an account of the proceeds. Five of us worked on the farm, yet he would still say that our earnings are deducted from loan,” Hari Ram said.He alleged that his children were also made to work and that the family was denied freedom to leave.“I was kept in severe bondage and suffered immensely,” he said. “Mere bacche anpadh hi reh gaye” (My children remained illiterate), he added, alleging that restrictions on movement prevented them from obtaining identity documents for children and enrolling them in school. The complaint about the family’s situation was filed by Hariram’s brother-in-law on Sept 28.However, Bikaner SDM Sanwarmal Regar said, “The complaint appeared to be motivated. Sharecropping is practiced in this area, and our investigation found no evidence of bonded labour. The person who filed the complaint does not reside in the area. We rescued the family and directed the farm owner to send them home. The family had come to work under a sharecropping arrangement, and no case of bonded labour was established in our inquiry.”In Ajmer, a father and his 15-year-old son were rescued on Oct 1. Shivraj Bheel had allegedly borrowed Rs 45,000 for medical expenses in 2023, after which his son was sent to work as a cow keeper. Shivraj later joined him when the debt amount allegedly rose to Rs 75,000 with interests. He said the owner refused to let him return home when his father suffered a heart attack in Sept 2026, prompting him to file a complaint against the owner on Sept 30. articles.title: How overcoming endometriosis transformed one Worcester woman's life
articles.summary: Carys Thurlby says "intense pain had become my normal" but surgery changed her life.
articles.body:
A woman who lived with "intense" pain from endometriosis for decades has lost more than half her body weight after surgery transformed her life.

Carys Thurlby lost 10 stone (140lbs) in 18 months after having a hysterectomy, which she said finally brought lasting relief from years of pain and exhaustion.

The 43-year-old said the change had been "night and day".

"Having intense pain had become my normal," she said.

Thurlby believes she had been living with endometriosis since she started her periods as a teenager.

She remembers sitting her GCSE exams "chewing on paracetamol" as pain spread through her pelvis and legs.

"I didn't really know that being in so much pain each month was not normal," she said.

"I didn't really know that what I was experiencing wasn't what women were meant to experience."

City redevelopment could include major NHS facility

She was diagnosed at 19 after undergoing a laparoscopy when she was in "excruciating" pain.

"That was the first time I had ever heard of it," she admitted.

Like many women with endometriosis, Thurlby spent years living with symptoms. The condition , which can affect multiple parts of the body, can have a major impact on work, education, relationships and day-to-day life, and there is currently no cure.

Over the years, she had several operations, but the effects were only temporary.

Her ovaries were eventually removed after being damaged by endometriosis, before she later had a hysterectomy.

Thurlby, from Worcester, said chronic pain and fatigue affected every aspect of her life as she balanced raising her children with her career.

"I can't describe how different it felt and it was a real shock to me to understand this is how normal people function, and not to accommodate pain and fatigue into everyday life."

She said she often relied on sugar for a quick burst of energy just to get through the day.

"The idea that I would then go out and exercise or move, even a gentle walk to the shops, was just not on the cards," she said.

"There was no room in my life for me to look after my wellness."

As her health improved, the weight began to come off. She gained confidence, started exercising and discovered a passion for running.

Eighteen months ago, she could not run for longer than a minute.

Since then, Thurlby said she had completed the Worcester Half Marathon and is now training for next year's London Marathon.

Her experience is shared by Vicki Shattock, from Belbroughton, who has written a book about her own struggle to have health concerns taken seriously.

Shattock urged women experiencing persistent pain to trust their instincts.

"You know your body better than anyone," she said.

"If someone is telling you pain is normal and you know it isn't, don't let it go."

articles.title: Service increases access to mental health support in East Yorkshire
articles.summary: The programme covers a range of topics, including managing anxiety and boosting self-esteem.
articles.body:
People struggling with their mental health and wellbeing are being encouraged to access free support ahead of World Mental Health Day.

East Riding of Yorkshire Council said its Wellbeing for Us programme, aimed at residents aged 18 and over, was designed to help people build confidence and make meaningful social connections, while reducing isolation.

The programme includes face-to-face workshops and informal peer support social groups and covers a range of topics, including managing anxiety and stress and boosting self-esteem.

The council said the programme also aimed to help residents access wider support, including community organisations, NHS referrals and other health services.

Workshops are currently being delivered on a rolling basis in Withernsea, Hornsea, Bridlington, Beverley, Driffield, Pocklington, Goole and Hessle, with drop-in sessions taking place in Goole and at Lelley Fields Crematorium.

Informal peer support social groups are being held in Goole and at Lelley Fields Crematorium, with more planned, the council said.

World Mental Health Day takes place on 10 October.

articles.title: Nepal floods: 10 missing as Budhi Gandaki River washes away 6 bridges in Gorkha
articles.summary: At least 10 people have been reported missing after flooding along the Budhi Gandaki River basin in Nepal’s Gorkha district early Sunday.
articles.body: At least 10 people have been reported missing after flooding along the Budhi Gandaki River basin in Nepal’s Gorkha district early Sunday. The floodwaters swept away six bridges, damaged several settlements and forced residents to flee to safer areas.The flood struck the northern part of the district around 4 am, officials said. Authorities are monitoring the river as its water level continues to fluctuate, while security personnel have been mobilised for search, rescue and evacuation operations.Assistant chief district officer Netra Prasad Sharma told ANI that 10 people had been reported missing since the flooding began.“In addition, 10 people have been reported missing since the flood hit the northern part of the district earlier this morning. An alert is in place as the river’s water level has continued to rise and fall. We are constantly monitoring the flow,” Sharma added.Six bridges swept away, houses damagedThe flood swept away six bridges, including two motorable bridges and four suspension bridges, according to officials. Bridges at Arughat, Tripurasundari and Soti-Manbu were among those reported damaged or destroyed, Sharma said.A Bailey bridge connecting wards 1 and 3 of Dharche Rural Municipality was also swept away. Other affected crossings included footbridges linking Machhikhola with Karauja, Thadobharyang with Jagat, and Ghattekhola with Philim.Nearly 35 houses in Painyu and Bagar in Ward 3 of Chumnubri Rural Municipality were swept away. Settlements in Jagat, Salleri, Dovan and Ghattekhola were also damaged.Also read: Nepal cuts 12 year wait, to declare those missing in flood 'dead' after 45 daysChumnubri Rural municipality deputy chair Laxmi Gurung said the flooding had caused extensive damage to the local market.“The Budhigandaki flood is reminiscent of the Bhotekoshi flood,” she said, according to Online Khabar. “It has washed away dozens of houses. It is not possible to say the exact extent of the damage right now.”Residents of riverside settlements, including Chumling and Lokpa, fled their homes after hearing loud roaring sounds from nearby streams around 4 am. Tourists staying at local hotels also left for safer areas, residents said, PTI reported.Nepal Army deploys teams for rescuePrime Minister Balen Shah said a Nepal Army contingent had been deployed by air and land to conduct search and rescue operations.Helicopters were also mobilised to support relief and evacuation efforts, while a joint rapid response team from Kathmandu was airlifted to the affected area.The Nepal Army later said six people had been evacuated to safer locations. The affected region is around 184 km from Kathmandu.Home minister Sudan Gurung said security personnel, including helicopter teams, had been deployed to assist with rescue and relief operations. He also warned that the river’s flow was continuing to rise and that muddy floodwaters had entered some houses in Ghattekhola.In a social media post, Gurung expressed concern over the destruction of the bridge connecting Nyakchet and Film Bazaar in Ward 3 of Chumnubri Rural Municipality.He urged residents of Sirdibas, Jagat, Salleri, Khorlabesi, Machhakhola, Soti, Arkhet and Arughat, particularly those living along the Budhi Gandaki riverbanks, to move to safer areas immediately.He also asked the people requiring emergency assistance to contact the ministry of home affairs on 1234. Authorities were also using loudspeakers to warn riverside residents and urge them to evacuate.This flooding in Nepal comes after the devastating Bhote Koshi River floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa district on August 26. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), the floods in the Rasuwa and Trishuli river areas claimed 1,455 lives, while 5,285 people remained missing.Authorities in Gorkha are continuing to monitor the Budhi Gandaki’s water levels as rescue teams work in the affected areas and residents are urged to remain alert.You use AI every day. articles.title: From Poonamallee to Vadapalani: PM Narendra Modi launches first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Phase 2
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Rail Phase-2 connecting Poonamallee Bypass and
articles.body: CHENNAI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Rail Phase-2 connecting Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani by flagging off the first driverless train at Porur Bypass station.The Prime Minister purchased a paper ticket at the counter, and took a train ride from Porur Bypass station to Poonamallee Bypass station and back, accompanied by chief minister C Joseph Vijay.The 15km elevated stretch, part of Corridor-4, has 11 stations and was built at a cost of Rs 4,900 crore. It connects the western suburbs to the existing Metro network at Vadapalani, where commuters can interchange with Phase-1 services.Regular passenger services will begin at 4pm today. articles.title: Pak crisis: Shehbaz govt declares emergency, ends Imran Khan's party's rule in KPK
articles.summary: Pakistan on Sunday declared an emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), suspending the provincial government led by jailed former prime
articles.body: Pakistan on Sunday declared an emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), suspending the provincial government led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party amid deteriorating law and order and a growing confrontation with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government.President Asif Ali Zardari issued the proclamation under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, citing rising terrorist attacks and a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the province. The move strips the elected provincial administration of its powers, with the chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general required to vacate their offices.The decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release and access to medical treatment for the former prime minister, who has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. The party has described the cases against him as politically motivated. The emergency also follows failed negotiations between PTI and the federal government over the planned protest.Terrorism, law and order citedThe presidential declaration said the emergency had been imposed because of the grave security situation and the provincial government's alleged failure to tackle militancy.“The extraordinary intensity of terrorist incidents poses serious threats to the lives and property of the public,” the declaration stated.PTI protests, warns of bloodshedPTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment. KPK chief minister Sohail Afridi is leading the protest march, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 and has passed through several districts.The party had initially planned to take the march to Islamabad for a sit-in, but authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to the capital and other locations. Two rounds of talks between PTI and the government failed to break the deadlock.Zulfikar Bukhari, a close Khan aide and PTI spokesman, called the emergency a “ridiculous decision”, saying KPK had the country's “only legitimately elected government”.“This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage,” he said, adding that there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent, with security personnel and civilians killed during demonstrations in 2024.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City’ star Angie Katsanevas is spilling her hair care secrets — she hopes her castmates are taking notes
articles.summary: The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City’ star Angie Katsanevas shares her favorite Kérastase hair care and travel must-haves from Skims, SkinCeuticals and more.
articles.body: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. She may have technically started as a “friend of,” but Angie Katsanevas has really always been a snowflake-holding member of “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City.” She never fails to make viewers laugh with her iconic one-liners and props (who could forget the scroll from season five), but she balances her humor with sincerity as she shares her Greek-American heritage, as well as her role as a caring friend, supportive mom and serious business woman. And this season, which is currently airing on Bravo every Wednesday, Katsanevas says she’s excited for viewers to get to know her even better. “We never know what they’re going to show, but there’s a lot of things I get to share in my personal story this season,” says Katsanevas. Standout moments include spending time with her daughter, Elektra, and her dad, who’s about to turn 90, as well as going behind the scenes of her business, the Lunatic Fringe Salon franchise. Katsanevas, who’s been a hairdresser for decades, even went to Washington D.C. earlier this year to testify before Congress on behalf of small businesses, becoming the first Housewife to do so. I recently caught up with Katsanevas, who shared some of her all-time favorite products, including a few that you’ll recognize from memorable moments on the show. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. One thing about Katsanevas is that her hair is always perfectly shiny, smooth and frizz-free — and she’s more than happy to tell you her secret to getting it that way. “I’m Kérastase girl,” she says, which all RHOSLC fans know — after all, the brand is mentioned in some of the show’s most famous scenes. “I love the products because they give you hold, softness and volume, but your hair can still move. I think we’ve gotten away from stiff hair — high body count hair, if you will,” says Katsanevas, referencing one of her most viral one-liners. “I’ve tried a million other things, and I’ve never been able to replace Kérastase to give you that timeless, beautiful blowout.” Katsanevas’ salon, Lunatic Fringe, has carried Kérastase products and offered its professional treatments for about 30 years. She also personally works with the brand, and especially loves its Chronologiste line. “It’s a luxury hair care line that’s anti-aging,” she says. “It helps fight signs of aging like dryness, dullness and lack of volume or thickness, which a lot of women battle as their hair changes. I’m going to be 53, and to have these products is pretty incredible.” Her top pick is the Chronologiste Overnight Youth Serum, which she puts in her hair before bed to work while she sleeps, and her other must-have is Kérastase’s Mousse Bouffante. Whether she’s traveling with family or her Housewives castmates, Katsanevas says packing her favorite things is essential to sleeping and resting well. Something that goes into her suitcase first is Skims pajamas, which you’ve seen her wear numerous times on the show. “I’m obsessed with them,” she says. “My daughter Elektra got me into them — she said, ‘Mom, they feel like a hug,’ and they do. They have the perfect weight to them, and now I can’t sleep without my Skims jammies.” “When I’m going on ‘Watch What Happens Live,’ I don’t want a crease in my face for having slept wrong and have my wrinkles on display, so I take my Slip Silk Pillowcase with me everywhere I go,” says Katsanevas. “It makes a huge difference for my hair and skin.” The machine-washable pillowcase is made from 100 percent pure mulberry silk, and it has a zipper closure to help it stay on your pillow as you move through the night. “I used to not travel with all my skin care because I didn’t want to pack everything, but I have to have certain products, and this is one of them,” says Katsanevas about SkinCeuticals’ vitamin C serum. She applies it every morning, and its main active ingredient, 15 percent L-ascorbic acid, helps correct the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, discoloration, loss of firmness and brightness, according to the brand. SkinCeuticals also says the serum is effective for at least 72 hours once it absorbs into your skin. These under eye patches are another one of Katsanevas’ skin care essentials. She uses them pre-glam to hydrate, de-puff and smooth out her skin, or she puts them on after taking off her makeup to reset her skin and feel refreshed before bed. The patches are made with ingredients like hyaluronic acid, ceramides, collagen and caffeine, and after wearing them for about 15 minutes you remove them and pat the remaining serum into the skin. Hosting is in Katsanevas’ blood. She has distinct memories of her parents, grandparents and aunts using their finest china whenever the family got together, and putting that kind of effort into hosting is something she’s always prioritized. “When people come into my home, I treat them like family,” says Katsanevas. “I love beautiful dishes, and tea cups, and servingware and having flowers out — I think it really adds to the experience. I know I go over the top, even if it’s just a little coffee date — like this season, when the women were coming over in the first episode, I went out and bought some really beautiful new appetizer plates. We’ve all gotten so busy, so people put out paper plates and cups, but the little details make it feel more beautiful. It’s fun when you have friends that notice it, like Mary [Cosby], and I want to teach Elektra to set the table, slow down and realize that it’s all part of the experience.” Katsanevas says she plans to buy her daughter, an avid equestrian, Hermes dishes from the Cheval d’Orient line to start her collection of fine china. “You’re passing down something beautiful, and you’re also passing down a memory for generations,” she says. articles.title: Modi is in trouble
articles.summary: The CJP protests sweeping through the country have exposed India’s hollowed-out democracy.
articles.body:
It is said that if you pluck a chicken one feather at a time, nobody notices. That is how some people deceive themselves into believing that small wrongs will never catch up with them.

The trouble with this method is that, one fine day, the truth stands bare, impossible to ignore. This October, Indian democracy resembles a plucked chicken, stripped of its plumage, as protesters who ironically call themselves “cockroaches” swarm our streets.

A lot of feather-plucking went on for 12 years before Prime Minister Narendra Modi found himself cornered, retreating behind barricades, facing the wrath of students for whom the slow erosion of democracy has left little to lose and even less to fear.

Confronted with a major protest on October 10 demanding the reversal of a purge of the voter rolls, he went on a self-incrimination spree. His government imposed measures reminiscent of the emergency era: no trains to New Delhi, paramilitary forces deployed at protest sites, the internet disrupted.

Ahead of the demonstration, leading figures linked to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest movement – Ratna Singh, Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee – were detained. Many other known activists, including Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson Tushar Gandhi, were also detained.

Regardless, demonstrators poured into the streets of New Delhi, trying to reach designated protest sites, in a scene that repeated in city after city across India. Through the day, the police played an endless game of whack-a-mole with the protesters, who kept resurfacing across the capital city, reassembling in one corner after another, driven from the designated protest sites but unwilling to disappear.

By the evening, at least 2,500 protesters and 15 journalists were detained across the city and taken to detention centres set up in various locations. Many have since been released.

These acts further erode the tenuous position Modi is in, prompting more rebuke from critics who now question his fitness to occupy the office of the prime minister. On Friday, the opposition parties, led by Rahul Gandhi, met President Draupadi Murmu and submitted to her that the government had subverted India’s democratic framework.

Under Modi’s watch, problems have accumulated like barnacles on the side of the ship. Every time he has been challenged, he has gone farther away from the democratic principles on which this nation was founded.

The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls – the last feather he plucked – was an exercise in bureaucratic fascism. There is simply no other way to frame an event that strips 130 million Indians of their right to vote.

The fact that this process helped sway elections is no longer up for debate. That the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, who oversaw SIR, is not resigning – out of shame – is astonishing. Even more so now that a corruption case from 2006 against him has resurfaced.

The chaotic, angry, defiant tableaux in the streets of New Delhi and beyond represent a reckoning that has been long in the making. The young, diverse protesters are a stark contrast to Modi and his cabinet – old, humourless men, who have bet on a strategy of demonisation and exclusion to succeed. His cabinet is filled with men full of self-importance, who had, mistakenly, wagered that crimes of elected officials should be tolerated and that a country can be governed indefinitely by creating fissures and manufacturing enemies.

We have now seen what happens when breakers of the law become makers of law. Criminal behaviour has been the organising principle of the party, and together, the values of these people have defined the years that Modi has ruled India. In the process, he has presided over the shredding of the Constitution of India.

Now that all this has come back to haunt him – in the form of “cockroaches” he is unable to exterminate – Modi has turned New Delhi into a fortress and unleashed all the power he has at his disposal on unarmed protesters. This is consistent with his policy of pretending to aspire to peace but unerringly generating conflict throughout his tenure: with neighbouring nations as well as among neighbours within cities.

October 10 is just an opening salvo. Over the next few weeks, Modi’s troubles will likely deepen. The CJP has announced protests will continue. Opposition parties have said they will protest on Monday.

The “cockroaches” seem to have resolved any remaining questions regarding Modi’s utter ineptitude as prime minister. They have laid bare the hollowed-out democracy that India holds up to the world as exemplary.

As his rule draws to a close — for now, the writing is on the wall — it can be safely said that history books will cast Modi in his proper role as the man who caused an entire generation of Indians to lose all respect for the government, the army, the Delhi Police, as well as the whole structure of governance.

New Delhi is temporarily suspended in a transition between a suffocating present and a promising future. This particular scrap of time, no matter how hard, will pass.

When that dust settles, what will become of all the institutions destroyed by regulatory capture and right-wing ideology – only those on the streets today will answer. This understanding is implicit in everything the “cockroaches” do. Because the whole point of it is power to the people.

articles.title: Pope Leo announces he will undergo surgery to remove lung nodule
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV has announced he will undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule that was discovered during recent health checks.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV has announced he will undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule that was discovered during recent health checks. The 71-year-old pope made the announcement to those gathered in St. Peter’s Square for the Angelus prayer on Sunday. “It was detected at a very early stage and is well-defined. The doctors deem it advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it.” A lung nodule is a small mass of dense tissue on the lung and most are non-cancerous. But risks can rise with factors like age. The Vatican said that the procedure was scheduled for early next week and that he would need a week in hospital to recover. During this period the Vatican will continue to function as normal, but decisions needing the pope’s signature will be placed on hold. Leo is relatively young for a pope, and is generally seen to be in good health. He plays tennis and remains physically active. Health problems dogged previous popes with Leo’s predecessor Francis spending an extended period in hospital and facing multiple health difficulties in the final months of his life. Leo XIV is preparing for a major visit to Latin America from 6-17 November where he is scheduled to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The pope has a demanding daily schedule of meetings and public events, although on Tuesday takes a day off at the papal retreat of Castel Gandolfo. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni offered her support to Leo “as he faces this challenge in the coming days.” This story has been updated.

articles.title: Riyadh airport attack another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
articles.summary: The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabian soil, and while the physical damage can be quickly repaired, its reputation for stability is taking a battering.
articles.body:
Saturday's attack on King Khalid Airport in Riyadh is another dangerous moment in a region that is already fraught with tension and conflict.

In recent weeks the Houthis have stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabian soil, but their attacks over the past few days have hit the country's critical infrastructure in the form of the capital's main airport , apparently penetrating Saudi air defences with ease.

The physical damage can be quickly repaired, but the country's reputation as a safe haven of stability is taking a battering.

As well as all the airport attacks, the Houthis have sought to take control of strategically significant positions along the Red Sea coast and around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. This further increases the risk to safe navigation along the vital maritime corridor - although the Yemeni government says it has "secured" the strait .

The civil war in Yemen between the country's government - which is internationally recognised and supported by Saudi Arabia - and the Houthis, who are backed by Iran, has been going on for more than a decade. It has left many thousands of people dead and plunged Yemen into one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

It is a complex and often confusing geopolitical conflict, and this latest escalation needs to be seen in the broader context of the tension between Iran, the United States and Israel.

Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

Houthi attacks raise fears of wider Middle East conflict and more global economic damage

Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

Not since the al-Qaeda insurgency of the mid-2000s has the Kingdom faced such a serious threat.

The Saudi government overcame that challenge through an effective hearts and minds campaign. Then it weathered the Arab Spring uprisings around the region which saw off leaders in Tunisia, Libya, Egypt and Yemen.

It even shrugged off – with some annoyance – an Iranian ballistic missile attack on Riyadh in March.

But this is different. Saudi Arabia may have one of the most powerful air forces in the Middle East, and it has been carrying out devastating air strikes on Houthi positions. Despite this, the opposing forces have managed to seize large portions of the country, particularly in the north and west.

But the Houthis know exactly where to hit back: at the soft underbelly of the Saudi economy.

As part of the " axis of resistance ", the Houthis are a vital strategic partner for Iran. From Jizan on the Red Sea to the petrochemical complex at Khurais, the Houthis are delivering explosive drones and missiles with deadly accuracy.

The Red Sea shipping route has become increasingly important, because the Strait of Hormuz, on the other side of the Gulf, has still not fully reopened since the US and Iran have failed to reach a deal to end their war .

Targeting ships in the Red Sea is another way that the Houthis are trying to exert leverage - the attacks cause global economic damage, which is a key bargaining chip for Tehran.

In early September, the White House stated it would not directly intervene in the Yemen conflict, but could provide intelligence support to the Saudis. It later confirmed that it was supplying intelligence and had deployed military experts to Saudi Arabia.

However the situation may have taken a new turn following the latest attack on Riyadh, which killed a US citizen.

Speaking to reporters, US President Donald Trump called Saturday's attack "terrible" and indicated he may intervene militarily with the Saudis.

"We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," Trump said.

But that now seems unlikely, at least before crucial US midterm elections next month.

When he was re-elected in 2024, Trump promised to end America's role in wars around the world. Despite this, the US is currently involved in three unresolved conflicts in the Middle East - in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

Should Trump get embroiled in another one, this time in Yemen, it is unlikely to go down well with voters.

This war now looks like it will intensify before it ends in another shaky truce - with or without US involvement.

articles.body: An NYPD detective who was stabbed and slashed seven times during a brazen Bronx robbery has been released from the hospital and is recovering from his injuries. "I’m feeling much better, thank you," Det. Jose Mercedes, a 10-year NYPD veteran assigned to the 44th Precinct, told the New York Post on Saturday. Mercedes, 33, was off duty Oct. 2 and cleaning out the trunk of his car in when two suspects allegedly ambushed him and tried to steal his gold chain, according to the NYPD. The suspects allegedly ripped the chain from his neck and fled on a motorized bike, sources and police told the Post. Video obtained by the newspaper showed Mercedes covered in blood as he was loaded into an ambulance after the attack. He was rushed to Jacobi Medical Center and released several days later. Mercedes was greeted Monday evening by dozens of fellow NYPD officers as he left the hospital in a wheelchair, with bagpipes playing and officers applauding. He later stood up, smiled and flashed a thumbs-up to the crowd. EXCLUSIVE: LEGAL GROUP TELLS NYPD COPS THEY CAN CONTACT ICE DIRECTLY DESPITE BLUE CITY'S SANCTUARY RULES Police identified the alleged attackers as D’Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24. Caraballo was identified as the alleged slasher, while Mejia was accused of driving the bike, according to the NYPD. Both suspects were identified by federal authorities as illegal migrants from the Dominican Republic. They were found hiding in the basement of a home in Lynn, Massachusetts, and taken into custody by the U.S. Marshals Service, the NYPD said Wednesday. articles.title: Abbas delays Palestinian elections again, making more than two decades without vote
articles.summary: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas delayed elections to 2027, extending a nearly 20-year wait as Israel and Hamas clash over the blame.
articles.body: More than two decades after being elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has once again postponed elections, extending a nearly 20-year wait for voters to choose a new legislature. Abbas issued a decree Friday pushing Palestinian Legislative Council elections from next month to Sept. 11, 2027, according to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA. Presidential elections, which have not been held since Abbas' 2005 victory, are also scheduled for that date. The delay allows Palestinian leaders to remain in power without facing voters and could further damage the credibility of the Palestinian Authority, which has faced criticism over corruption and its security cooperation with Israel. NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION The Palestinian Authority, dominated by Abbas' Fatah party, governs parts of the West Bank under agreements reached in the 1990s. Palestinian officials cited conditions in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and east Jerusalem as reasons for postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, claimed Israel had blocked election materials and international observers from entering Gaza, according to The Associated Press. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar rejected the claim, accusing Abbas of trying to shift blame for the delay. Abbas' "attempt to drag Israel into this, falsely claiming that Israel imposed obstacles to holding elections, is yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability," Saar wrote on X. Hamas, meanwhile, welcomed the postponement, calling it "a step in the right direction" and urging further talks on rebuilding Palestinian institutions before holding elections. Palestinians last held legislative elections in 2006, when Hamas won a majority of seats. Israel and Western countries subsequently boycotted the Hamas-led government, fueling unrest that ended with Hamas taking control of Gaza in 2007. IRAN REAFFIRMS SUPPORT FOR HAMAS AS TRUMP PUSHES TO DISARM TERROR GROUP Since then, Hamas has controlled Gaza while Abbas' Fatah-dominated Palestinian Authority has governed parts of the West Bank. The postponed election also threatened to bring new challenges to Abbas' leadership. Before the delay, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and a faction led by Mohammed Dahlan, a former Fatah security chief who fell out with Abbas, had been discussing an unlikely political alliance. "Abbas is terrified by the electoral alliance bringing our faction together with opposition factions and forces within Fatah that reject his leadership," Dimitri Dilliani, a spokesperson for Dahlan's faction, said in a statement. The decision comes as the Palestinian Authority's future role in Gaza remains uncertain under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire plan reached last year. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The plan calls for the authority to eventually play a role in Gaza, but its immediate responsibilities remain unclear. Hamas continues to govern the territory, while a committee of Palestinian technocrats remains in Cairo awaiting permission to enter Gaza and oversee a transition of power.
